item_description_text: Groundhogs are fast, smart, chubby rodents with thick brown fur, short legs, and strong claws. They are a species of marmots which are closely related to squirrels. Groundhogs dig tunnels in the dirt to make underground homes called burrows that usually have one main entrance and one or more escape exits. Groundhogs look for food in open areas like prairies and yards and at the edges of forests. They eat grasses, flowers, seeds, fruits, vegetables, and nuts, getting as thick as they can before they hibernate, which they can do for up to eight months–far longer than most animals. Groundhogs were living four million years ago during a long, cold time called the Ice Age, which may be why they developed such long hibernations. Today, groundhogs live across much of the United States and Canada and are sometimes called woodchucks or whistle pigs.
sources: Evolution of the Rodents, ch 9 pg 248 https://www.bio.fsu.edu/steppanlab/assets/files/Polly%20et%20al%20Marmota%20chapter%20Evo%20of%20Rodents%20proof.pdf
